segments.en: Entries 61–66: Money as root of all things, arrogance, and craft as contraction. Money answers everything because at its root money comprises all powers — the supernal colors from which all creation flows through a chain of cosmic loans. With holy wealth the tzaddik and their followers receive the illumination of the supreme will; with unholy wealth idolatry holds. In money is the essential trial of arrogance which includes all middos. All crafts are contractions that must be sweetened through their specific intellect rooted in supreme wisdom — through Torah study.

Entries 67–80: The two faces of wealth, faith, three repairs of commerce, and the soul-basis of acquisition. Holy wealth flows from the Yam HaChachma and illuminates the faces; wealth of one who disputes the tzaddik becomes the vessel of idolatry. Giving money to true tzaddikim elevates wealth to holiness. Tzedaka clarifies the imagination and restores memory. Fallen fears = Amalek = livelihood burden. Holy wealth requires guarding the bris; subduing materiality like a donkey-under-load earns holy wealth. Wealth from questions one overcomes; Torah studied for its own sake draws pure wealth. A peruta is the measure of both monetary and faith significance. Commerce has three repairs: faith in speech, Torah in thought, spark-clarification in action. Unlawful taking of another's money leads to blemishing the bris. All acquisitions are soul-exchanges; money acquires by Torah law because it is the root of souls; a written document completes the innermost soul-transfer.

Entries 81–84: Impudence, soul-roots of property, sun and moon. Holy boldness resides in money; wealth used for tzedaka repairs one's money and produces holy boldness to defend the righteous and achieve complete teshuva. The root of land is the Written Torah, movable property the Oral Torah. The moon borrows from the sun; faith-blemish = moon-blemish = poverty and loans. When Israel does Hashem's will they lend to nations and do not borrow.

Entries 85–87: Good days and bad days; transmigration and justice. The essential trial is finding good within the bad days — Torah letters are clothed even in languages of the nations. Failure to find them causes contraction of flow and loans. Teshuva requires finding the good even within the evil — one who wishes to return must guard against debt. Poverty and coveting flow from the secret of soul-transmigrations — there may be an ancient debt between souls. Yet Torah forbids touching what is not one's own; one must accept Hashem's judgment with love.

Entries 88–91: Hashem's glory, daily sustenance, and the worker's wage. Every Jew must believe they are a source of particular glory to Hashem each day — and this is the basis of daily sustenance: the flow drawn to each person corresponds to the glory ascending from them. Giving the worker's wage on the same day reveals glory, draws daily flow. Poverty from not giving tzedaka; kindness and charity restore the flow to Israel. Returning the pledge garment corresponds to light and darkness cycles of glory. Essential wealth through repairing justice; essential poverty through its blemish.

Entries 92–96: Commerce as Mishkan-building; the fire of judgment; poverty and loans. Commerce properly conducted builds the holy sanctuary — the sparks within it are converts and penitents. The fire of self-judgment (hisbodidus) burns the evil in the sparks; without it, anger comes and ruins wealth. Poverty strips the mind, leading to further justice-blemish in a vicious cycle — tzedaka broadens the poor person's mind and can break the cycle. In exile, the Beis HaMikdash is held as pledge. Sparks in money = clarification of prayer; Temple levels correspond to the stages of clarifying possessions from mountain and field to house — Third Temple will never be pledged.

Entries 97–100: Commerce as descent-for-ascent; ayeh; hidden and revealed. Commerce is a necessary descent for ascent — one must seek ayeh (where is the place of His glory?) during worldly engagement, which corresponds to the sealed saying. Land = fixed revealed holiness; movable property = hidden, mobile holiness of the sealed saying. All debts = not yet clarifying the four elements = servitude even after death. Dying in debt = transmigration. The full trial of livelihood is the hidden-and-revealed dynamic — Hashem hides and reveals His face. One who maintains faith in both "the whole earth is full" and "ayeh" merits holy livelihood; denying another's money flows from making a separation between these two comprehensions.

Entries 101–108: Moon-blemish, three intellects, and the true tzaddik. Lending is filling the moon's blemish — the central tikkun. Repaying restores Malchus to its root. Commerce intention: earn money to give tzedaka to reveal the colors and break imagination = ascent in Torah. Three intellects: in-potential (cash), in-actuality (merchandise), acquired (land). Debt repaid with coins because colors in holy money break the imagination. Acquired intellect = the deed = what survives death. Holy commerce illuminates the colors = Mishkan. Complete prayer binds to the true tzaddikim = lender not borrower. Loans from prayer-blemish. Holy wealth = completeness of deficiencies, only through the true tzaddik; Haman-Amalek = the false teacher who always lacks.

Entries 109–120: Robbery, anger, faith, and the will. Robbery blemishes the power of Creation — a just judge is Hashem's partner in Creation. Just judgment makes a great unification and is the basis of Redemption. Poverty = fallen fears = debt-fear = servant's fear. Holy wealth = subduing anger; the wealth of Esav/Haman is itself anger — temporary like a storm. Tree of Knowledge = gold, silver, bronze = money is the battleground of good and evil. Money-desire from anger = Egypt exile. Sparks clarified through faith, which draws power from Torah — "a Torah matter is acquired by coins." Faith = legs = money — poverty = stumbling. Kinyan (legal acquisition) was instituted only to strengthen faith. All debts = action, serpent's defilement, servitude; repaying = returning to will. Money = kesef = yearning and will. Complete tzedaka would nullify all commerce — work done by others. All acquisitions in commerce draw the will's illumination, compelling faithful fulfillment.

Entries 121–122: Kinyan sudar, Moshiach, and the World to Come. The kinyan sudar draws the spirit of Moshiach — the source of faith. The essential service of all one's life-days is cleaving to the World to Come, and the essential expression of this is commerce with faith. The first question after death — "Did you deal faithfully?" — is actually the question of how much one cleaved to the World to Come.

Entries 123–128: The makifim, happy with one's portion, and not forcing the moment. All livelihood flows from the illumination of the surrounding lights (makifim) which the true tzaddik draws through da'as. Just as one must not draw makifim beyond one's current soul-level, so one must not force livelihood before its time. Each time one's deficiency is filled a greater one emerges — happiness with one's portion is the only remedy. Wealth given before its time = wealth guarded for one's detriment. Hashem calibrates each person's livelihood precisely for their level of free choice. Denial of another's money = outright apostasy from faith.

Entries 127–129: Chok, garments, and deep mysteries of commerce. Livelihood must be received as a divine statute — beyond questioning — always rejoicing in one's portion. All denials flow from faith-blemish. The essential money-desire comes from looking only at the externality of garments on money. Every business arrangement contains wondrous mysteries of Providence and soul-roots — cast everything upon Hashem. The Sitra Achra seizes through garments (Bava Metzia opens with "two hold a garment"). The oath in monetary disputes reveals the supernal colors and repairs truth.

Entries 130–133: Mezuza, guarding another's property, letter-combinations, and prayer. The mezuza drives away outer forces from the entry-point of flow and draws abundance inward. Guarding another's money (even from visual damage, returning lost objects) repairs the holy vessels through which G-dliness shines, repairs the bris, and draws the tzaddik's Torah-light. All crafts involve letter-combinations — Betzalel knew how to combine the letters of Creation. The root of all crafts is prayer; all trades are derived from the Mishkan = house of prayer. The early Chassidim's piety preserved their Torah and blessed their work. All damages flow from prayer-blemish; truth guards from all damages.

Entries 134–137: Evil eye, livelihood burden, partnership, and foolish deviations. The evil eye flows from entering forbidden questions (why does this person have what I lack?). The burden of livelihood = burden of sins from foolishness; holy da'as sheds both. Most commerce done through partnership because each Jew must illuminate da'as in their companion — this is the root of all partnership and the reason "the mazal of two is better." All commercial fraud is pure foolishness — "deceit does not prosper." Kinyan sudar's garment draws the makifim's da'as, nullifying the spirit of foolishness.

Entries 138–140: Truth in commerce, sparks from outside to inside, and tzedaka saves from death. The great darkness in commerce requires truth as remedy — truth illuminates openings in the darkness. Commerce = war to extract sparks; connection to true tzaddikim as householder is essential. Intend in all commerce to give tzedaka to Torah scholars. The ultimate completion of wealth is bringing it from outside to inside the house. Tzedaka gathers soul-scattering and saves from death.

Entries 141–146: Partnership as soul-union, commerce as war, supporting Torah scholars, and the great fall. Commerce's root is the conflict of wills between buyer and seller; kinyan sudar elevates sparks (converts) under the wings of holiness and brings peace. Commerce must be connected to Torah (Zevulun-Yissachar model). Commerce is a great war — partnership pools the holy power of the bris. Supporting Torah scholars = wielding the staff of strength, enabling joy and spark-clarification. Deviations flow from Sitra Achra idolatry in money; repair = bris-guarding and love of Israel. Money-desire is the greatest fall and hardest from which to rise; Hashem sends tzaddikim to support us; ultimately Moshiach will purify the world.

Entries 147–160: Left within right, prophetic imagination, sparks and acquisitions. Wealth flows from the left which must be included in the right (faith in Providence = left within right = splitting of the Reed Sea). Commerce clarifies faith-sparks; kinyan sudar's garments = the holy imaginations of prophets = clarification of imagination = repair of faith. The supernal colors in holy silver and gold flow from the Garden of Eden. All acquisitions elevate sparks from level to level; ona'ah blemishes da'as and reverses the clarification. Forcing the moment blemishes da'as and makes livelihood heavier. Essential livelihood = good counsel from Hashem, not toil and anxiety. Going out to the market = wilderness of serpents; the sukka-shelter of peace (from Shabbos) guards one. Ona'ah mixes good and evil further. Commerce repair = the tzaddik's point = Yosef. The 28 letters of Creation = Torah letters = the power and vitality of all property; the document (shtar) embodies this. A gift's root is free kindness before Torah; sustaining of world = revelation of Torah. Most acquisitions through silver = breaking the shells surrounding the sparks; one who hates gifts will live.

Entries 161–162: Na'ase v'nishma and the ultimate point of truth. All commerce flows from the same root as na'ase v'nishma — making the hidden revealed. Therefore one ought to stand by one's word, and one who does not displeases the Sages. The shekhiv mera's words carry legal weight because at the moment of departure the completeness of speech finally prevails. One who reaches the ultimate point of truth — knowing there is nothing besides Hashem — is not considered dependent on creatures even when receiving from them.

Entries 163–166: Money-desire as the Greek kingdom; guarding; the tzaddik of each generation. All commerce is the World of Action where idolatry holds strongest; tzedaka is the remedy. Money-desire is the Greek kingdom defiling all oils of da'as. The true tzaddikim of each generation gather Israel's tzedaka-merit to draw a generous spirit that breaks money-desire and renews Torah. One must guard earned money like the apple of one's eye — Yaakov returned for small vessels. Complete Providence flows through the tzaddik's Torah innovations and sustains Israel.

Entries 167–169: Compassion, Shabbos unity, and supporting Torah scholars. The burden of livelihood = burden of sins from foolishness; receiving holy da'as lifts both. Showing compassion and speaking words of fear of Heaven to another draws livelihood to them; judging favorably draws livelihood. The Simple One's unity flows through varied actions — Shabbos draws rest onto all weekday affairs. Remedy for burden: abandon hatred and dispute, seek love and peace. Blemishing money by chasing self-desire and disputing Torah scholars separates the varied actions from the Simple Unity and causes apostasy.

Entries 170–172: The first question on Judgment Day; Mishkan-work; Malchus and voice. The first question — "Did you deal faithfully?" — asks whether all commerce was directed toward repairing faith or at minimum through tzedaka to Torah scholars. All actions for livelihood = contractions drawing divine spirituality = work of Mishkan and Creation. One who accepts Torah's yoke fully — work done by others; essential drawing is through Torah and the true tzaddikim. Creation was for revealing Malchus; all wealth is from the aspect of Malchus; "honor Hashem from your throat."

Entries 173–175: Guardians, Shabbos truth, and two types of damage. Israel's money = portions of holy Malchus; damage = Malchus-blemish; guarding = Malchus-repair. When an object is separated from its owner the Sitra Achra holds more strongly. Four guardians correspond to four parts of speech; Shabbos holiness drawn into weekdays via truth in speech = guarding. Two categories of damage: (1) from kelipos rooted in the breaking of vessels — guardable by human intellect; (2) from kelipos rooted in the empty void — guardable only by faith and bitachon in Hashem.

Entries 176–178: Bitachon, the empty void, and the 140 voices. Essential livelihood flows from bitachon alone; yet human effort is needed to clarify sparks from the breaking of vessels. The counsel of what to trade = clarification from the empty void = only through faith and bitachon. The effort itself = clarification from the breaking of vessels. Torah warns against saying "my strength made this." Before knowing any counsel = the empty void; faith precisely there draws good counsel. Money flows from the contraction of the empty void; therefore all 70 forms of idol-worship are embedded in money-desire. The Shechina cries 140 voices (2×70) over one who falls into money-desire. Repair = complete faith that the empty void is from Hashem for revelation. Spending money generously for tzedaka and mitzvos = expressing this faith. Buying mitzvos with full silver = complete faith that the void is full of G-dliness. Avraham's Cave of Machpela and David's threshing floor — both bought with full silver — reveal holiness from the void through complete faith expressed in generous spending.

Entries 179–184: Faith as complete guarding; Malchus-da'as vs. wicked kingship; the two types of heretics. Complete faith that money flows only from Hashem guards from damages beyond human prevention. All theft and robbery = wicked kingship = foolishness; guarding = holy Malchus = da'as. Torah guards scholars completely. Depositing with others is difficult — the essential guarding is connecting the externality of every thing to its inner holy intellect. Torah innovations by true sages sweeten all judgments and guard the world's wealth. The essential warning of love of companions: don't be jealous of another's money. Two types of damage = two types of faith-blemish. Two types of heretics: pleasure-seeking (cause theft/loss) vs. serpent's-forehead cruelty (cause robbery/compulsory harm).

Entries 185–188: Faith in sages, freedom from servitude, encompassing intellect, and bitachon. Wealth flows from the left (judgments); faith in sages completes Torah and sweetens judgments; Zevulun-Yissachar model. Blemishing faith in sages leads to servitude; faith in sages leads to freedom — "engraved on the tablets = freedom." The root of all flow = supreme encompassing intellect; each person's vessel = their intellect; faith in sages perfects the intellect-vessel. Love and peace among Israel includes all intellects in the encompassing intellect, opening all channels. Dispute blemishes all intellects, channels become confused, Israel's flow goes to the nations. No remedy except returning to faith in sages. The essential deficiency of livelihood = deficiency of da'as; the only remedy even in bitter exile is strong bitachon. Entry 188 ends with the beginning of Rebbe Nachman's quoted words — the passage is not reproduced in this compilation. Entries 189–190 are absent from this source.

Entries 191–200: The Will, Torah as shield, craftwork, and faith as the root of everything. Damages flow from denial of the Will (natural scientists); faith in the Will nullifies all damagers. Two types of heretics correspond to two types of damage. Revelation of the Will brings livelihood without effort; money = the Will's clothing; subjugating money to Hashem's Will guards it. Torah reveals that Hashem created all, and created all for Israel — nullifying the damagers' claim of "robbers." Free chesed of the great tzaddik guards those idle from Torah; the unpaid guardian is exempt because they did free chesed. Complete Torah-blemish → compulsory damage; Torah-study interrupted → must sustain through Torah hidden in worldly occupation; connected to the true tzaddik → even during commerce guarded from theft/loss. All things come from Above incomplete — human craft completes them = Tree of Knowledge clarification = bris-repair = livelihood. Torah is itself the ultimate craft (amon). One who hates ill-gotten gain has precious holy money = holy Malchus; four guardians correspond to Malchus's four; chesed elevates Malchus from the four evil kingdoms and guards all wealth. Israel's holy money flows from very high and illuminates lower wisdom. The root of all crafts and the guarding of everything = faith.

Entries 201–204: The two aspects of bris; holy and evil yearning. Lower bris = knowing permitted/forbidden = scholar = six weekdays = commerce. Upper bris = full tzaddik-aspect = Shabbos = all blessings come through this. Effort alone accomplishes nothing; wealth comes only from before Hashem. The true tzaddik needs no work; all is done by others. One must connect all commerce to the tzaddik (Shabbos-aspect). Two types of damage correspond to the two aspects of bris. Evil yearnings — especially when verbalized — cause the Sitra Achra to hold on one's flow; holy yearning through the tzaddik and Shabbos reverses this.

Entries 205–212: Holy money as glory; memory as guarding; breaking money-desire for complete Providence. All wealth contains sparks of holy glory — Yaakov elevated glory in Lavan's house. Israel's money is very precious and its guarding elevates glory to its root, drawing world peace. Personal and general peace nullify all damages. The essential guarding of money = guarding the memory (cleaving to the World to Come) = remembering Hashem in commerce — "remember and guard in one utterance." Livelihood flows more easily according to how much one remembers. The manna was gathered "in foolishness." Paying the worker's wage on that day = repairing the memory through sparks. Servitude = serpent's defilement; freedom = illumination of the Will = forgiveness; even a day-laborer cannot bear servitude — wages must be paid immediately. Toiling by one's hands draws the Will's illumination and is greater than simple fear of Heaven. Complete Providence = breaking money-desire; money-desire blocks complete Providence.

Entries 213–224: Torah, theft, da'as, and double flow. Breaking money-desire = drawing Torah = raising mayin nukvin. The thief removes Providence from the world and is ready for all sin. Livelihood is doubly as difficult as childbirth — 70 voices for birth (revealing da'as), 140 voices for livelihood (descending through two stages to physical form). Connecting money to da'as draws double flow and nullifies money-desire. Separating money from da'as = dust, no life, never having half one's desire. The Shechina's cry of "my head, my arm" = the two stages. Israel's money = double flow from Shabbos. The thief denies Providence and must pay double. Two cries of seventy = breaking the two stages of evil. Money-desire causes wondrous fall = destruction of Temple. Mashiach repairs money-desire. Clothing the naked saves from money-desire. Lifting the Torah nullifies money-desire. An object leaves a domain only through despair + change of act = the two stages. The tzaddik uses holy "theft" (stories) to awaken fallen souls and draw double Torah-flow = double wealth.

Entries 225–235: Sweetening contractions; robbery; commerce sustains the world. The completeness of mitzvos requires spending money. Each person can only sweeten their own contractions — robbery intensifies judgments; the flood was sealed by robbery. All Torah = sweetening contractions; robbery = the complete opposite = blemishes the entire Torah. Acquisitions require lifting to the supernal root (foundation stone, Holy of Holies) where all intellects and contractions are unified. Commerce = lifting things to their supernal root. Sandal removal at the Temple = the same principle. Commerce with faith, in connection with true tzaddikim, literally sustains the world. Robbery destroys the world. Robbers pay according to the time of robbery — time itself is essentially nothing; falling under time = money-desire = foolishness. All unintentional damage = blemish of anger = blemish of da'as. Visual damage = heart-desire = falsehood = da'as-blemish. Damages of Israel's money = destruction of the Temple (from foreign wisdoms entering the brain). Israel in exile fed from dregs; the true tzaddik is poor while the world eats from their merit; every Jew must return livelihood to its First Master.

Entries 236–260: Holy money, the informer, the bris, and the coming of Mashiach. All damages = blemish of faith and bris. Israel's money = a well of living waters growing holy faith; money-desire = a pit of snakes and scorpions (apostasy). The informer hands over Israel's holy money to the nations — the greatest possible desecration, literally making holy money into idolatry, blemishing all Torah, destroying Creation's vitality. Israel's money has the supernal colors = the glory Hashem takes in Israel = ascending from level to level. The informer's status = apostate, worse than Shabbos-violator. Disputed Israel money = strengthening the Sitra Achra's kingship against holy Malchus. Most disputes are about money; peace depends on not chasing money. Money's root is very high holiness = the Sitra Achra holds there most strongly = greatest potential for both holiness and damage. The four evil kingdoms = four avos nezikin; collecting from the best = extracting swallowed holiness until only pure evil remains. Four elements = householder = river from Eden. Rising at midnight subdues the fire-causes. Holy brazenness (crown-ornaments of Chorev) subdues the Sitra Achra's brazenness = collecting from the best. Three tractates of Bava = "In the beginning G-d created" = repair of brazenness through Eden. Wealth flows from nine holy palaces formed by the Kesser restraining the rushing mochin = "crown of wisdom is their wealth." Joy draws wealth. Multiplying needs destroys life; all suffering and preoccupation with livelihood flows from withholding tzedaka. Money-desire and bris-blemish are interlinked; falling into money-desire is the worst fall. Tzedaka repairs both. Israel's money = holy = tzedaka. Flow root = mah → thousands → hundreds (= two hundred = double Providence = true wealth). Breaking money-desire = fulfilling the entire Torah = clarifying all sparks in silver and gold = paving the way for Mashiach = completing the bris. The soul's garment after death is formed from the holy sparks clarified through holy money and wealth.

The governing principle (entries 1, 4, 7, 20): Thought is always in a person's hand — this is the section's foundational axiom, repeated emphatically throughout. Two thoughts cannot coexist simultaneously. Therefore the entire battle with evil thought is not a fight but a displacement: think another thought, and the first is automatically expelled. Every hairsbreadth of effort to redirect thought is precious beyond measure before Hashem. Cumulatively, these hairsbreadths form the holy contractions through which divine attainments are drawn.

Flight, not combat (entries 2, 4, 19, 21): The Rebbe's central tactical teaching: never argue, negotiate, or engage with evil thoughts — arguing with the pursuer tells them you plan to flee. The model is Yaakov fleeing Lavan: steal away without looking back. The Sitra Achra is Pharaoh (Paro = exposure) who opens door after door for one who begins to be drawn in. But just as these doors opened, there are also doors out — illuminated by truth and by the true tzaddik. The moment of entry is the moment of freedom: flee immediately, do not look back.

The flood, the Land of Israel, and the bris (entry 3): Thought-confusion — especially of the illicit desire — is literally the Flood: the waters that wish to sweep away and destroy from both worlds. Eretz Yisrael was not flooded but some was splashed in. The purity of thought = the holiness of Eretz Yisrael = the repair of the bris. King David's many psalms about great waters are all about this. Only the tzaddik's paths of simplicity and wholeness can save from the flood.
